correctness.rationale: The exact partition product gives f(x)+f(rx). On y in [log r,3log r] the ratio f'(y/r)/[-r f'(y)] is positive, has logarithmic derivative 1-1/y+o(1)>0 uniformly, and goes from below to above one. Thus exactly one local minimum lies in the window. The stationary equation yields y=2 log r+log log r+log4+o(1) and heat capacity (log r)^2/r^2. The two side peaks follow by derivative sign changes at fixed small/large-gap Schottky peak neighborhoods. All 42 standalone finite diagnostics passed but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The valley separating two quantum thermal-excitation scales is a natural thermodynamic invariant. In contrast to the familiar individual peaks at temperatures proportional to each gap, the valley is controlled by matching the algebraic tail of one component against exponential suppression of the other and acquires a nontrivial log log r offset. Its precise position and vanishing height quantify resolution of widely split anomalies. No overclaim is made for finite ratios or interacting experiments.
